title: Malicious code in ukraine69 (PyPI)
description: The ukraine69 package on PyPI contains malicious code that executes during import. This code attempts to escape sandbox environments, locate Telegram bot session files, and trigger malicious account deletions. The campaign associated with this package is identified as malicious with destructive actions and attempts to cover tracks.
aiSummary: The ukraine69 PyPI package versions 1.2.0, 1.2.1, 1.2.2, 1.2.3, 1.2.5, 1.2.6, 1.2.7, and 1.2.8 contain embedded malicious code that activates upon import. The code is designed to bypass sandbox restrictions, search for Telegram bot session files on the host system, and initiate unauthorized deletion of accounts. This behavior classifies the package as part of a malicious campaign named 2026-10-ukraine69, with clear intent to perform destructive actions and conceal its activity.
aiImpact: Users who install and import the affected ukraine69 package versions risk unauthorized deletion of Telegram bot accounts and potential compromise of their environment due to sandbox escape attempts. This can lead to loss of access and data associated with Telegram bots and possible further system compromise.
